title: Active-active gateway: streaming session failover and graceful traffic shedding
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
We operate a globally distributed hosted API using an anycast edge + regional gateway clusters. Most workloads are short requests, but we have increasing traffic from long-lived streaming sessions (SSE/WebSocket/HTTP chunked). We need an active-active failover model that preserves SLOs (latency, availability) while handling streaming session semantics and avoiding cascading failures during regional overloads.

Goal:
Design and implement an active-active traffic strategy for the hosted API edge/gateway that: (1) enables seamless failover for new and existing streaming sessions, (2) enforces per-region circuit breakers and load-shedding to protect tail SLOs, and (3) provides clear observability and runbook actions for on-call.

Non-goals:
- Full multi-master state replication for application-level session state (out of scope). We will rely on short resume tokens and lightweight session metadata replication where necessary.

Design decisions and trade-offs (summary):
1) Routing model: Anycast at the edge with region-hint headers. For session affinity we prefer deterministic hashing of session_id -> preferred-region; fallback uses global LB to route to healthy region. This minimizes cross-region traffic while allowing failover.
2) Streaming session handling: Two options considered: connection mirroring (expensive) vs. resume tokens + short-lived stateless checkpoints. We chose resume tokens and small session checkpoints persisted in a geo-replicated KV (primary: write-local, eventual cross-region replication) to keep cost predictable.
3) Circuit breaker placement: Combination of client-side and gateway-side breakers. Gateway-side breakers are per-route and per-region, triggered by 5xx rate, queue length, and resource saturation. Client-side SDK will respect 429/503+Retry-After for retry/backoff.

Key components to implement:
- Per-region health scoring service for LB weight decisions (metrics input: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, active connection count, CPU/GPU util, queue length).
- Weighted traffic shifting orchestration: gradual weight changes with alerts and automatic rollback on SLO violation.
- Streaming session resume flow: generate monotonic resume_token at connection start; persist minimal checkpoint (cursor, model, prompt prefix) in geo-replicated KV; on reconnect the client sends resume_token and preferred-region hint; gateway attempts local restore, otherwise proxy to region with checkpoint within TTL.
- Circuit breakers + load-shedding policies: per-route thresholds and hierarchical actions (soft-shed: reduce batch size / lower QoS model; hard-shed: reject with structured error and Retry-After).
- Observability/dashboards: new SLO-focused dashboards and per-region connection overview.

Operational rules and SLOs:
- Global API availability SLO: 99.95% (excl. maintenance). Regional availability SLO: 99.9%.
- Streaming session SLOs: p50 end-to-end first-chunk latency < 120ms, p95 < 500ms for edge-attached sessions; Resume success rate >= 99.5% within TTL window.
- Circuit-breaker triggers (first pass): 5xx-rate > 1.0% sustained over 1 minute OR active connections > 120% of provisioned for 30s OR avg queue length > 200 -> start hard-shed policy.

Load shedding and fallback policies (prioritized):
1) Graceful deprioritization: lower-tier customers and background ingestion routes get reduced concurrency and slower batch sizes.
2) Model degradation: automatically fall back to cheaper/less resource-intensive model variant for non-critical requests (configurable per-tenant).
3) Reject with structured error for traffic that cannot be served while returning Retry-After and a high-level reason code ("region_shed", "global_overload").

Streaming-specific considerations:
- Long-lived TCP (WebSocket) connections cannot be migrated. We will rely on: (a) resume tokens + quick reconnect, (b) client SDK exponential reconnect with region hint, and (c) attempt to keep same public session id so the resumed session uses previous conversation context.
- For server-sent events and chunked HTTP we will prioritize preserving last-good checkpoint before forced termination.
- Connection draining: on region scale-down or planned maintenance we will stop accepting new streams, allow existing streams to finish for a short drain window (configurable: default 20s), then trigger client reconnect with resume guidance.

Client SDK changes and compatibility:
- Add support for resume_token and explicit X-Region or prefer-region header. SDKs will auto-reconnect to preferred region for resume.
- Accept 307/302 redirection semantics only for non-streaming requests; streaming reconnects should use resume flow, not 307.

Observability and runbook:
- Dashboards to add: per-region active streams, resume success rate, avg resume latency, per-route circuit-breaker state, shed count/time, SLO burn rate heatmap.
- Alerts: automated page if resume success rate drops > 0.5% within 5m OR region health_score < 0.6.
- Runbook (high-level):
  1) Identify affected region(s) via dashboards.
  2) If health_score degraded, begin weighted traffic shift away by 10% every 30s until below threshold or until a max 90% shift.
  3) If SLO burn or error spike continues, enable hard-shed for non-critical routes and notify Product for prioritized customer handling.
  4) For streaming sessions, request customers rely on SDK auto-reconnect; provide status page messages and exp-backoff guidance.

Compatibility test plan and rollout:
- Unit + integration tests for resume token lifecycle, KV checkpoint write/restore, and simulated reconnects across regions.
- Chaos test: stage fail a region in staging and verify automatic weight shift and resume rate >= 99%.
- Canary rollout: enable the traffic manager for 1% traffic routed with new health scoring and shedding rules, monitor for 48 hours, then 10%, then 100% if stable.

Open decisions / risks:
- Geo-replicated KV consistency: current cluster uses eventual replication with potential 2–5s lag; risk of resume token not yet replicated. Mitigation: set resume TTL to 60s and prefer local region for short writes. Consider using sync replication for critical session writes later.
- Cost vs. UX: more aggressive mirroring would reduce resume failures but increase cost. We chose a pragmatic resume-first approach to keep costs acceptable.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Active-Active+Streaming+Failover
- Draft architecture diagram: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/streaming-failover-arch.png
- Initial PR (staging plumbing): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2819

Acceptance criteria:
1) Resume flow works end-to-end in staging with a simulated inter-region failover and achieves >= 99.5% resume success.
2) Circuit breakers fire and recover automatically in a controlled stress test without human intervention.
3) Dashboards show correct per-region metrics and alert on defined thresholds.
4) Canary rollout completes with no SLO regressions at each step.

Next steps / action items:
- ENG: implement health scoring service and LB weight API (owner: Miguel).
- SRE: add circuit-breaker config to gateway and implement soft/hard-shed handlers (owner: Evelyn Park).
- SDK: publish resume-token support and region-hint behavior in 2.1.0 release (owner: Zoe Chen).
- PM: prepare customer communication templates for streaming disruption scenarios (owner: Priya Nair).

runbook_summary: If a region's health_score declines: 1) shift traffic away gradually by LB weights; 2) enable per-route soft-shed, monitor SLOs; 3) if streaming impact high, enable hard-shed for background routes and page SRE; 4) provide resume guidance to customers and monitor resume success metric.
acceptance_criteria: Resume flow >= 99.5% in staging under simulated region failover
Per-route circuit-breakers trigger and recover automatically during stress tests
Dashboards and alerts present and validated by SRE
Canary rollout steps succeed with no SLO regressions
